talk_track: Barry Hess here — I spent 16 years as CTO of a defense SDVOSB getting a patented tactical platform from prototype into operators' hands in theater, then watched it die force-wide for lack of a senior champion inside the building. Scout's Director of Engineering posting defines the job as 'ensuring that Scout's payloads, flight software, and data products are delivered on time, meet mission requirements' — and on the same board, the Capture Manager req asks one hire to build 'companywide processes to ensure consistent success in capturing new business' from scratch. Read together, those postings say the TACFI clock is now the company clock: months-to-orbit has to beat the funded months remaining, and the capture muscle that turns a Phase II into a Phase III is being assembled mid-flight. In my experience the engineering is rarely what kills a transition — it's fielding architecture and acquisition advocacy sequenced after the build instead of alongside it. Which arrives first for Owl — the orbit date or the Phase III decision?
